messages:
Jessica (Support): FYI a customer reported a sharp spike of 504s from eu-central for hosted inference around 11:03 UTC. They say it started ~11:01 and lasted ~6m. Attaching the short repro they gave.
Mia (SRE): Can you paste the exact curl they used and any request IDs?
Jessica (Support): curl -v --max-time 10 'https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED' --data '{"prompt":"hello"}'
Jessica (Support): Customer logs show repeated `504 gateway timeout` and these request IDs: req_eu_11: 0a3f9d, req_eu_12: b9c1f2, req_eu_13: 5d2a01
Arjun (NetEng): I'm seeing BGP withdraws from ISP-AS64512 to our eu-central POP at ~11:00:59 UTC, short AS path changes then flaps for ~45s in the provider feeds. Could be transient path change causing packet reorder/loss. Pulling netflow and peering logs now.
Mia (SRE): Correlating with our metrics: increased tail latency on gateway frontends in eu-central-1a and 1b, packet retransmit rate up ~12x on eth0 of edge nodes. Also observed a small spike in TLS handshake timeouts.
Luca (Infra): HAProxy frontend logs from one affected host (haproxy-euc-17):
```
Apr 07 11:02:58 haproxy-euc-17 haproxy[1234]: 192.0.2.45:52344 [07/Apr/2026:11:02:58.123] frontend/post 0/0/10000 504 502 - - ---- 3/3/0/0/0 0/0 {"rid":"0a3f9d"}
```
Mia (SRE): That 10s in the log looks like our internal timeout firing after retries. We see intermittent 5xx from upstreams likely due to in-flight KV cache misses plus packet loss causing streaming stalls.
Arjun (NetEng): Provider reported a microburst and automatic reroute to a longer path, AS path length increased then recovered. They flagged an interface flap at their edge. I'll open a ticket but mitigation first: add temporary BGP community to prefer alternate peer and withdraw traffic from the affected interface. Can ops flip peering-preference?
Luca (Infra): We can push a short-lived route preference change via our interconnect controller. Rolling a change now to steer traffic to peer2 in eu-central. Will notify when done.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1873 - eu-central provider reroute affecting hosted inference - severity: P2
Mia (SRE): After steering, error rate fell back to baseline ~11:09 UTC on all frontends. Customer confirmed service recovered ~11:10 and could repro that requests succeed.
Jessica (Support): Customer asked if this could affect billing or auth. They saw some retries and a single 504; no auth errors. Billing shouldn't be impacted aside from token usage on successful retries. Notifying them of mitigation and that we're opening a provider escalation.
Arjun (NetEng): I'll share the provider ticket ID and AS path dump in the incident doc. Short term mitigation: keep peer2 preference for 30m, then revert if stable. Also adding more conservative TCP retransmit on egress for edge hosts to reduce upstream timeouts.
Mia (SRE): Action items: 1) Arjun - provider escalation + ticket ID in pager duty doc. 2) Luca - keep steering for 30m and monitor. 3) Jessica - customer comms + note on billing. 4) SRE oncall - watch for recurrence and capture pcap if it does.
Jessica (Support): Thanks, sending a note to the customer: "We observed a short provider-level reroute causing packet loss and increased latency in eu-central. We steered traffic to an alternate peer and service recovered within ~8 minutes. We're escalating with the provider and will follow up with the ticket details. No auth or billing errors observed beyond retried requests." :thumbsup:
Mia (SRE): Closing thread here, will link to postmortem if provider confirms root cause. If anyone sees recurrent spikes, re-open and drop pcap/pcap-ng to the incident thread.
Arjun (NetEng): Provider ticket: TKT-87921 opened. AS path before: 64512 3333 4444 -> after flap some routes via 64513 7777 4444. I'll add dumps to the incident doc.
Luca (Infra): Monitoring note: added a temporary dashboard panel for retransmits and per-AZ TLS handshake failures. Keeping this on for 2 hours.
Jessica (Support): Customer replied: "Thanks for quick response, happy to see recovery. Please keep us posted on root cause."
Mia (SRE): ack, marking resolved for now.
